newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 17.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Thursday:
* Barely nine months after he was recruited to lead the nation's largest telephone company, John Walter stepped down as president and chief operating officer of the AT&T Corp.
* Anti-smoking advertisements in California have not stopped teen-agers from starting to smoke.
* ITT Corp said it would split itself into three separate companies and buy back $2.1 billion of its stock.
* Consumer prices rose only one-tenth of one percent in June.
* General Motors and Ford announced better-than-expected earnings.
* Apple Computer reported a smaller-than-expected loss.
* Time Warner and U.S. West ended their talks to disband their cable TV and entertainment venture.
* Popularity of the Internet and wireless telephones fueled strong earnings at Lucent Technologies.
* Northrop Grumman and General Dynamics reported bigger-than-expected earnings gains.
* PresidentClinton waved for the third time provisions of the Helms-Burton Act.
* New York State officials approved a partial state takeover of Long Island Lighting.
